summary: Independent review confirmed the original AST-rewriter overhead on the prepared base and verified that candidate b96c5b615d9ca62ef023836af4f858bd3f0c5b7e removes unnecessary control-flow transformer traversals while preserving the supported control-flow transformations. In this environment, a fresh-process 1,000-statement straight-line rewrite retained identical behavior and reduced the median measured transform time from 38.606 ms to 18.487 ms; Transformer.visit calls fell from 40,031 to 1. The candidate is a justified Python-only optimization and is not merely test hardening.

Base median 38.605626 ms with exactly 40,031 Transformer.visit calls per sample; candidate median 18.487033 ms with exactly 1 call per sample. Both returned the same numerical result, 1002. gpu_execution_evidence: The candidate executed examples/01-vectorAdd.py on the assigned AMD GPU and printed PASS. The emitted final ISA starts with .amdgcn_target amdgcn-amd-amdhsa-unknown-gfx950 and defines vector_add_kernel_0.
remaining_limitations: The optimization is entirely in python/flydsl/compiler/ast_rewriter.py, so no C++ native rebuild was applicable; Python imports resolved to /job/repo/python/flydsl/compiler/ast_rewriter.py and native bindings remained the image-prepared pinned build. GPU and ISA validation covered the available gfx950 architecture only, not every supported AMD architecture. The source issue states only a general optimization request and no target workload or acceptance threshold, so the cold synthetic benchmark isolates frontend AST rewrite cost rather than claiming an end-to-end compilation speedup for all kernels.
